title: OLTP and OLAP: different workloads demand different models

videos.script: A bookshop sells a book. The till writes one order, two lines and a payment, in one short transaction. {{till}} At the end of the month, somebody asks how much each department sold this year against last. That question reads every line the till ever wrote. {{report}} Same data. Same database, if nobody stops to think. And the two jobs want opposite things from it. {{same}} The till wants small tables, one fact in one place, and an index that finds a row in a handful of pages. The report wants to read millions of rows, a few columns of each, and it wants history the till threw away when a customer moved or a price went up. {{opposite}} This lesson runs both against the shop's own PostgreSQL, measures them, and then asks the same question of a warehouse built for it. {{measure}} Same answer, to the cent. Very different cost. The rest of the course is how that second database is designed, and why it looks the way it does. {{course}}
